name: Mang Den pig
summary: VietnamNet describes a free-range pig of Măng Đen, also called heo rẫy, roasted whole over charcoal. The same article writes “Heo Măng Tây” once in that description. Go Vietnam’s Măng Đen article describes a different cut: Sedang black pig on skewers.
origin: VietnamNet’s 14 July 2023 article lists the Măng Đen roast among Kon Tum specialties. Go Vietnam describes Sedang black pig in Măng Đen.
taste: VietnamNet says the meat is fragrant and firm because the pigs eat wild feed and range, and the largest adult is under 20 kg. Go Vietnam says the Sedang black pig is firm and sweet.
howToEat: VietnamNet: clean the pig, season it with củ nén, sawtooth herb, coriander root, lemongrass, and chili, and roast it whole over charcoal until the skin is golden and crisp. A price was not printed on that article.

Go Vietnam’s Măng Đen article: Sedang black pig on skewers with chili salt and forest leaves, at 250,000–400,000 VND a plate. That is a different cut from the whole roast. Both stay. Check on arrival.
where: Măng Đen, Kon Plông. VietnamNet ties the whole roast to that plateau. Go Vietnam ties the skewers to Sedang cooking there. A city-market stall in Kon Tum was not printed. Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Mang Den pig — whole roast and skewers
seoDescription: VietnamNet describes a whole charcoal roast of the Măng Đen pig, under 20 kg. Go Vietnam prints Sedang skewers at 250,000–400,000 VND a plate.
